intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Arrive mid-morning after settling in nearby accommodation to make the most of the afternoon sun. Ideal for swimming, sunbathing, and light water sports. Renting a sun lounger and umbrella keeps costs low while maximizing comfort.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine Tasting at Quinta dos Vales
experiences.description: Visit Quinta dos Vales, a renowned estate winery near Estômbar, offering guided tours and tastings of award-winning Algarve wines including Syrah and Touriga Nacional blends. Book a morning session to allow time for other activities in the afternoon. The estate is centrally located in the Algarve, making it easily accessible from Lagos or Portimão hotels, minimizing travel time.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear waters of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Walk the scenic coastal trail from Benagil and descend to the beach for a swim. Staying in Carvoeiro or Lagoa puts you within 10 minutes of this spot, eliminating long travel days and making it easy to arrive early before crowds build.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle into the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most photographed natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing from Benagil Beach. Tours typically last 1.5 to 2 hours and are best done in the morning when seas are calmer and light filters beautifully through the cave's oculus. Operators are based directly on Benagil Beach, making this highly accessible from Lagoa or Carvoeiro accommodations.

experiences.name: Adega do Cantor Winery Tour and Tasting
experiences.description: Tour the celebrity-owned Adega do Cantor winery near Guia, famous for its Vida Nova and Aneto wine labels. The estate offers intimate guided tastings with panoramic vineyard views and is conveniently located near Albufeira and Lagoa, making it a perfect half-day afternoon activity. Pairing the visit with a nearby beach morning creates an ideal full-day itinerary without excessive driving.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport at 13:00. Take the affordable bus or shared shuttle to Lagoa (approx. €5-8). Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll around Lagoa town center to get your bearings. Visit the charming Igreja Matriz de Lagoa church and explore the local market square.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the quiet streets of Lagoa old town in the early evening. Head to a local tasca (traditional tavern) for a simple but authentic Portuguese dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport or on arrival for under €3
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bifana (pork sandwich) or tosta mista at a local café in Lagoa for €3-5
meals.dinner: Tasca O Zé or similar local tavern in Lagoa — grilled fish of the day with bread and salad for €10-13

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on arrival, settling in, and orientation. Buy a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data (€10-15). September weather in Algarve is warm and sunny, typically 25-28°C — perfect beach weather.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most beautiful and accessible beaches near Lagoa (approx. 10 min by local bus or cheap taxi). Arrive early to claim a good spot on the golden sand. Swim in the warm Atlantic waters and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs framing the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the scenic Carvoeiro boardwalk along the cliffs to the Algar Seco rock formations — a stunning natural sea cave and rock pool area, free to visit. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it. Explore the small rock pools and arches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus. Enjoy a sunset stroll in Lagoa and visit a local wine shop to pick up a bottle of Algarve regional wine (€5-8) to enjoy at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local padaria (bakery) — coffee and toast with butter and jam for €2-3
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl) and eat on the beach — €4-6 total
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro or a simple grill house in Lagoa — grilled sardines or piri-piri chicken for €10-14

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is free to visit and one of the most photogenic spots in the Algarve. Wear reef-safe sunscreen. Buses between Lagoa and Carvoeiro run regularly and cost under €2 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Silves, the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve, just 10 km from Lagoa by local bus (€2). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) with panoramic views over the orange groves and river valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (Igreja da Sé) and the Archaeological Museum (€2.10 entry). Walk along the Arade River banks and browse the local craft shops. Visit the Silves market if it falls on a trading day for fresh local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Lagoa. Visit a local adega (wine cellar) or wine bar in Lagoa for a tasting of Algarve wines — look for Quinta dos Vales or local cooperative wines at very affordable prices.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — galão (milky coffee) and croissant for €2.50
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at Marisqueira Rui or a local tasca — cataplana de peixe (fish stew) shared between two for €12-15 per person
meals.dinner: Simple dinner at the hotel or pick up fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and Algarve wine from a supermarket for a budget picnic dinner — €8-10

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit historical gem. The castle is one of the best-preserved Moorish fortresses in Portugal. The bus from Lagoa to Silves is very affordable and scenic. September is harvest season in Algarve — you may spot fig and almond harvests.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Benagil, one of the most famous beaches in Europe, accessible from Lagoa by bus or bike. Take an affordable kayak or stand-up paddleboard rental (€15-20) to paddle into the iconic Benagil Sea Cave — a breathtaking cathedral-like sea cave with a hole in the ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coast to Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Walk the cliff-top trail connecting Benagil and Marinha for stunning views. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Relax and enjoy the town's evening atmosphere. Visit a local cervejaria (beer house) for a cold Super Bock draft beer and petiscos (Portuguese tapas).

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — fresh orange juice, coffee, and toast for €3
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar near Benagil or Marinha — grilled sardine sandwich and cold drink for €6-8
meals.dinner: Petiscos at a local cervejaria in Lagoa — chouriço assado (grilled chorizo), pataniscas de bacalhau (cod fritters), and beer for €12-15

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil Cave can only be accessed by water — swimming in from the beach is possible for strong swimmers but kayak tours are safer and more affordable (€15-20). Book in advance during September as it remains popular. Praia da Marinha requires a steep staircase descent.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine tasting morning. Visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (very close to Lagoa), one of the Algarve's most acclaimed wine estates. Book a budget-friendly wine tasting tour (€10-15 per person) to sample their award-winning reds, whites, and rosés among the vineyards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Estômbar village, a charming and often overlooked town near Lagoa. Walk to the Igreja de São Tiago and enjoy the peaceful riverside setting on the Arade River. Rent a bike locally and cycle the flat riverside paths.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Lagoa for a relaxed evening. Browse the local evening market if available, or enjoy a glass of wine purchased from the winery on the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local padaria — coffee and pastel de nata for €2
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery café or a picnic with local bread, local cheese, and olives bought at a supermarket — €6-8
meals.dinner: Restaurant A Churrasqueira in Lagoa or similar — half-chicken piri-piri with fries and salad for €9-12

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is one of the best wine estates in the Algarve and offers excellent value tastings. Call ahead to confirm tasting availability and times. The Algarve wine region produces excellent Negra Mole and Touriga Nacional reds. September is grape harvest season — a magical time to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Lagos, one of the Algarve's most beautiful coastal towns (30 min by train from Lagoa/Tunes station, €3-4 each way). Explore the historic old town, the Forte da Ponta da Bandeira, and the striking Ponta da Piedade limestone rock formations and sea stacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo in Lagos — two stunning beaches nestled between dramatic golden cliffs. Swim and relax. Walk the cliff-top trails for spectacular views. Explore the colorful Lagos marina area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos's vibrant evening atmosphere before catching the train back to Lagoa. Lagos has a great budget nightlife scene with lively bars and cheap drinks.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa before departing — galão and toast for €2.50
meals.lunch: Lagos market or a local café — grilled fish sandwich, bifana, or a prego (steak sandwich) for €5-7
meals.dinner: Dinner in Lagos before returning — Restaurante Adega da Marina or a local tasca — ameijoas à bulhão pato (clams) and grilled sea bream for €13-16

day_by_day.notes: The train from Tunes (near Lagoa) to Lagos is one of the most scenic and affordable ways to travel the Algarve coast. Ponta da Piedade is free to visit and absolutely stunning at golden hour. Wear sturdy shoes for cliff walks. Last train back to Tunes departs Lagos around 21:30 — check timetables.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a leisurely morning walk around Lagoa. Visit the Lagoa Municipal Market for fresh local produce, dried figs, almonds, and local honey — great for budget snacking throughout the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia de Armação de Pêra, a long sandy beach west of Lagoa (bus €2). This is one of the longest beaches in the Algarve — great for long walks, swimming, and people-watching. Visit the small whitewashed Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha perched dramatically on the cliffs nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the chapel ruins above Armação de Pêra cliffs. Return to Lagoa for a quiet dinner. Try cooking in if your accommodation has kitchen facilities using fresh market produce.

meals.breakfast: Slow hotel breakfast or local café — scrambled eggs, toast, juice, and coffee for €4-5
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Armação de Pêra — grilled sardines on bread with a cold beer for €7-9
meals.dinner: Self-catering using market produce (fresh fish, vegetables, local bread) or a simple tasca meal in Lagoa for €8-11

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally slower-paced — a mid-trip rest day. The Lagoa market is excellent for budget food shopping. Armação de Pêra is popular with Portuguese locals rather than tourists, giving it an authentic feel. The Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha is free to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip east to Albufeira, the Algarve's most famous resort town (bus from Lagoa, €3-4). Visit the charming old town with its whitewashed buildings, mosaic-tiled streets, and the Praça Túnel. Walk down to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in the old town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Praia da Oura and the surrounding cliff walks. Visit the Albufeira marina area and browse the local craft stalls. Take a short boat trip from the marina to see the sea caves and grottos along the coastline (budget boat tours from €15-20).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Albufeira's famous Strip (Rua Cândido dos Reis) for cheap drinks and a lively atmosphere before heading back to Lagoa by bus.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry in Lagoa before departing — €2
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local restaurant in Albufeira old town — grilled limpets (lapas) and a cold drink for €10-13
meals.dinner: Budget-friendly meal in Albufeira before returning — piri-piri chicken or a mixed grill for €10-13

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira's old town is far more charming than the touristy strip. Focus your time in the old town and on the beaches. The strip is fun for an evening drink but can be expensive — stick to local bars rather than tourist-facing cocktail bars. Bus back to Lagoa runs until late.

day_by_day.morning: Second dedicated wine experience. Visit the Adega do Cantor winery near Guia (between Lagoa and Albufeira), co-owned by Cliff Richard. Take a guided tour and tasting of their Vida Nova wines (€12-15 per person). The estate is set in beautiful countryside with orange and almond groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Guia village, famous for its frango piri-piri (piri-piri chicken) restaurants — a cultural institution in the Algarve. Walk around the village and visit the local church. Browse the roadside stalls selling local almonds, figs, and carob products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Enjoy a quiet evening on the hotel terrace with a bottle of Algarve wine. Reflect on the trip so far and plan any remaining activities.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local café — coffee and tosta mista for €2.50
meals.lunch: Frango piri-piri lunch in Guia — this is a must-do Algarve experience. A half-chicken with fries and salad costs €9-12 at one of the famous local restaurants
meals.dinner: Light dinner — local supermarket cheese, cured meats, olives, fresh bread, and a glass of wine from the winery visit — €6-8

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor's Vida Nova wines are excellent and the estate is beautiful. Book the tasting in advance. Guia's piri-piri chicken restaurants (Ramires is the most famous) are a genuine Algarve culinary tradition and very affordable. The chicken is marinated and grilled over charcoal — outstanding value.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Portimão, the Algarve's second-largest city (15 min by bus from Lagoa, €2). Visit the excellent Museu de Portimão (€3), a fascinating museum in a converted sardine canning factory telling the story of Algarve fishing heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo, a picturesque fishing village with colorful boats, a medieval castle (Castelo de São João do Arade), and beautiful beaches. Explore the village on foot and visit the small local fish market on the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Ferragudo's waterfront with a cold beer. Return to Lagoa by bus via Portimão. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — coffee and pastel de nata for €2
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ferragudo — fresh grilled fish at a waterfront restaurant. Look for the daily catch — dourada (sea bream) or robalo (sea bass) for €11-15
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Lagoa — bacalhau com natas (creamy salt cod bake) or carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) for €10-13

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most authentic and unspoiled fishing villages in the Algarve — far less touristy than Albufeira or Lagos. The Museu de Portimão is genuinely excellent and very affordable. The walk across the bridge from Portimão to Ferragudo is free and offers great river views.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final relaxed morning at Praia de Carvoeiro or Praia da Marinha — revisit your favorite beach for a long swim and sunbathing session. September waters are still warm (around 22°C) and crowds have thinned from summer peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — a stunning 5.7 km cliff-top coastal walk between Praia de Vale Centeanes and Praia da Marinha. This free trail offers the most dramatic coastal scenery in the Algarve with arches, grottoes, and hidden coves.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate near the end of the trip with a special budget-friendly dinner in Carvoeiro village. Browse the small boutique shops and artisan stalls in the village square.

meals.breakfast: Pack a picnic breakfast from the supermarket — yogurt, fruit, bread, and juice — €4
meals.lunch: Snack bar near the trail — grilled sardine sandwich and cold water — €5-7
meals.dinner: Dinner in Carvoeiro — Restaurante Boneca or a local grill house — mixed seafood grill or cataplana for €13-16

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is one of the most spectacular free walks in Portugal. Start early or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat. Wear proper walking shoes as the path has some uneven rocky sections. Carry plenty of water. The trail is well-marked and takes approximately 2-2.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Monchique, the mountain town in the Serra de Monchique hills north of Portimão (bus from Portimão, approx. €4). Explore the charming spa town of Caldas de Monchique with its mineral water springs, wooded valley, and traditional architecture. Hike up to Fóia, the highest peak in the Algarve (902m) for panoramic views over the entire region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Monchique town itself — visit the ruined Franciscan convent, browse the local handicraft shops selling wooden furniture and medronho (arbutus berry brandy). Try a shot of medronho at a local bar — a true Algarve tradition.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa via Portimão. Enjoy a final evening walk around Lagoa and start packing. Pick up local souvenirs — bottled medronho, local honey, dried figs, and almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo) are all affordable and authentic.

meals.breakfast: Early café stop in Lagoa before departing — coffee and croissant for €2
meals.lunch: Lunch in Monchique — traditional Algarve presunto (cured ham) sandwich or a local restaurant serving cabrito assado (roast kid goat) for €10-13
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Lagoa — choose your favorite restaurant from the trip or try Restaurante O Terraço for a local Algarvian spread — €12-15

day_by_day.notes: Monchique offers a completely different landscape from the coast — lush eucalyptus and cork oak forests, cooler temperatures, and mountain scenery. The medronho brandy is a local specialty and makes an excellent inexpensive souvenir. Check bus timetables carefully as services to Monchique are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Enjoy a slow breakfast and check out of the hotel. If time permits, take a final walk around Lagoa town center and visit the local café one last time for a farewell galão and pastel de nata.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, either head directly to Faro Airport (bus or shuttle, €5-8) or stop briefly at Faro old town (Cidade Velha) if time allows — explore the walled old city, the Roman arch, and the beautiful Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Assunção for free.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day budget adventure through the Algarve — stunning beaches, excellent wines, dramatic cliffs, and authentic Portuguese culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel or café breakfast in Lagoa — coffee, juice, and pastel de nata for €3
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Faro Airport or a café near the airport — prego sandwich or soup and bread for €5-7
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro Airport. The bus from Lagoa area to Faro takes approximately 45-60 minutes. Keep some euros for airport coffee or last-minute souvenirs. Total estimated daily budget per person: €50-70 including accommodation, meals, transport, and activities — very achievable in the Algarve in September.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Lagoa on foot. Visit the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (parish church), stroll through the local market square, and pick up snacks or wine at a nearby deli or supermarket to stock your room.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle first dinner in Lagoa town center — keep it relaxed after travel. Explore the pedestrian streets and enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine at a terrace café before an early night.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich at a café in Lagoa town center after check-in (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Leão in Lagoa — traditional Portuguese grilled fish and piri-piri chicken, mid-range (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 begins only after 13:00 arrival. Keep the day light to recover from travel. Ask hotel staff for local tips and restaurant recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most scenic beaches near Lagoa (~10 min drive). Swim in the calm September waters, explore the golden cliff formations, and walk the coastal boardwalk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Algar Seco — dramatic coastal rock formations and sea caves just east of Carvoeiro. Explore the natural arches and sea pools, then enjoy a drink at the clifftop bar overlooking the Atlantic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for dinner. Browse the lively restaurant strip along the beachfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local pastelaria — coffee, fresh orange juice, and pastel de nata (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a beachside café in Carvoeiro — grilled sardines or bacalhau (~€14–18)
meals.dinner: O Castelo restaurant in Carvoeiro — fresh seafood and Portuguese wine with ocean views (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal for beach visits — warm water, fewer crowds than peak summer. Bring sunscreen and reef-safe products for rock pool areas.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning at Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (~15 min from Lagoa). Book a guided vineyard tour and tasting of Algarve reds, whites, and rosés. The estate also features outdoor sculpture gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Silves, the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve (~15 min drive). Visit the imposing red sandstone Castelo de Silves and the Gothic Cathedral. Wander the cobbled streets and browse local artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves — a town known for excellent traditional restaurants along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café in Lagoa
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery café or a snack in Silves after the castle visit (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Café Inglês in Silves — beloved local restaurant inside the castle walls, serving cataplana and regional dishes (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking for tours. Silves castle entrance is approximately €3–4. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Benagil — take a boat tour from Carvoeiro (~10 min drive) to see the famous Benagil Sea Cave, one of the most photographed natural wonders in Portugal. Book in advance as tours fill up quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coast to Praia de Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Swim, snorkel among the rock formations, or simply relax on the golden sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a relaxed evening. Visit a local wine bar to try more Algarve wines and regional cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading to Carvoeiro for the boat tour
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — buy fresh bread, local cheese, olives, and fruit from a Lagoa deli (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Taberna do Marquês in Lagoa — cozy tavern serving petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and local wines (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Benagil boat tours sell out fast — book online 2–3 days ahead. Praia de Marinha has limited parking; arrive early or take a taxi. The cliff path to the beach involves steps.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão (~20 min drive). Visit the Museu de Portimão, an award-winning museum housed in a former sardine canning factory — fascinating insight into local fishing heritage. Free or low-cost entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha, Portimão's famous urban beach with dramatic orange cliffs and a long sandy stretch. Swim, walk the clifftop promenade, and explore the 16th-century Fortaleza de Santa Catarina.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner — the riverside quay is famous for charcoal-grilled sardines.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pastelaria in Lagoa
meals.lunch: Grilled sardines at one of the riverside quay restaurants in Portimão — a quintessential Algarve experience (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic in Portimão — long-standing local favorite for fresh seafood and cataplana (~€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Museu de Portimão is closed on Mondays. Praia da Rocha can get busy but September crowds are manageable. The riverside sardine grills are informal and excellent value.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Adega do Cantor winery in Guia (~20 min drive) — the winery famously co-founded by Sir Cliff Richard. Enjoy a guided tour and tasting of their award-winning Vida Nova wines amid beautiful Algarve countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Albufeira (~25 min from Lagoa) and explore the Old Town. Wander the whitewashed alleys, visit the Igreja de São Sebastião, and relax at Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in the town center.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Albufeira Old Town — lively atmosphere with many restaurant options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Tapas and wine at the winery or a café in Guia (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira — iconic seafood restaurant built into old ruins above the beach (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor tours require advance booking. Albufeira Old Town is pedestrian-friendly. Avoid driving into the Old Town — park at the edge and walk in.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed mid-trip morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time at the hotel. Use the pool or lounge area to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lagoa's local farmers' market (if open) or drive to the nearby village of Estômbar for a peaceful riverside walk along the Arade River. Spot local birdlife and enjoy the rural Algarve scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset wine tasting at the hotel or a local wine shop in Lagoa — pick up a bottle of Algarve rosé and enjoy it on your terrace or at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Local tasca (family tavern) in Estômbar or Lagoa — pork with clams (carne de porco à alentejana) or grilled chicken (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: O Barradas restaurant near Silves — rustic countryside restaurant famous for regional Algarve cuisine and local wines (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter as a mid-trip rest day. Use this time to do laundry, plan the second week, or simply decompress. A balanced itinerary needs breathing room.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos (~35 min drive west). Start with Ponta da Piedade — stunning golden sea stacks and grottos. Hire a kayak or small boat tour to explore the sea caves from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos Old Town — walk the ancient city walls, visit Igreja de Santo António (baroque church with gilded interior), and browse the artisan craft market near the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos, one of the Algarve's most vibrant towns with an excellent restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before driving to Lagos
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — fresh catch of the day with local wine (~€16–22)
meals.dinner: No Pátio restaurant in Lagos — intimate courtyard restaurant serving creative Portuguese cuisine (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade kayak tours should be booked in advance in September. Wear water shoes for the rocky shoreline. Lagos Old Town is compact and very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Meia Praia near Lagos — a long, wide, uncrowded beach perfect for a morning swim and walk. September offers warm sea temperatures (~22°C) with fewer visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Lagoa and stop at Quinta da Penina wine estate (~20 min from Lagoa). Enjoy an afternoon tasting of their Algarve wines in a beautiful estate setting.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar near Carvoeiro, followed by dinner back in Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Lagos before heading to the beach
meals.lunch: Beach café at Meia Praia — simple grilled fish, salad, and local beer (~€13–17)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo (~10 min from Lagoa) — excellent riverside seafood restaurant with views of the Arade estuary (~€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is a beautiful, less-touristy fishing village worth visiting for dinner. The riverside setting at sunset is particularly scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the historic town of Faro (~45 min drive east). Explore the walled Old Town (Cidade Velha), the Gothic-Manueline Cathedral (climb the tower for panoramic views), and the Arco da Vila.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro marina to Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) in the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a pristine barrier island with crystal-clear lagoon waters and unspoiled beaches. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for dinner before driving back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before driving to Faro
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch on Ilha Deserta at the Estaminé restaurant — the only restaurant on the island, serving fresh fish and shellfish (~€18–24)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Ricky in Faro — popular local spot for grilled fish and regional wines (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules to Ilha Deserta in advance — last return is usually late afternoon. Cathedral tower climb costs ~€3. Faro Old Town is a UNESCO-listed heritage area.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wine tour and tasting at Quinta do Morgado da Torre in Mexilhoeira Grande (~25 min from Lagoa) — one of the Algarve's most respected wine estates producing Alvor wines. Guided tour of the vineyards and cellars.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Alvor village (~20 min from Lagoa) — a charming fishing village with a beautiful estuary boardwalk, traditional whitewashed houses, and a great beach. Walk the 4km wooden boardwalk through the Alvor Estuary.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Alvor — the village has an excellent selection of seafood restaurants along the main strip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery or a café in Alvor village after the boardwalk walk (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Três Palmeiras in Alvor — beachfront restaurant renowned for fresh seafood and shellfish (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta do Morgado da Torre requires advance booking. The Alvor boardwalk is flat and easy — excellent for birdwatching in the estuary. Alvor village is very photogenic.

day_by_day.morning: Return to your favorite beach for a final full beach day — Praia de Carvoeiro or Praia de Marinha recommended. Spend the morning swimming, snorkeling, or simply enjoying the Algarve coastline one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Slide & Splash water park near Lagoa (optional, great for a fun afternoon) OR take a scenic drive along the EN125 coastal road stopping at viewpoints (miradouros) above the cliffs between Carvoeiro and Benagil.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable final evening meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — fresh seafood skewers, cold drinks, and local beer (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred fine dining experience, a special treat for the final evening (~€60–80 per person with wine pairings)

day_by_day.notes: Bon Bon is the Algarve's most celebrated fine dining restaurant — book well in advance. If budget is a concern, substitute with O Castelo in Carvoeiro (~€25–30). This is your last full day, so make it special.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagoa. Enjoy a slow hotel breakfast, pack your bags, and take a last stroll through Lagoa town. Visit a local deli or shop to buy Portuguese wine, ginjinha, or local honey as gifts or souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer to Faro Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of Algarve's golden cliffs, world-class wines, and fresh seafood home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy it slowly
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Lagoa before departure, or at Faro Airport (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Transfer from Lagoa to Faro Airport takes approximately 45–55 minutes by taxi or pre-booked transfer (~€35–45). Book your airport transfer the evening before to avoid stress. Check your airline's baggage allowance if purchasing wine bottles to bring home.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear waters of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Walk the scenic coastal trail from Benagil and descend to the beach for a swim. Staying in Carvoeiro or Lagoa puts you within 10 minutes of this spot, eliminating long travel days and making it easy to arrive early before crowds build.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 45 minutes). Settle into your suite, unpack, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely stroll through the charming town of Lagoa. Visit the historic Igreja Matriz de Lagoa and explore the local artisan shops along Rua 1º de Dezembro. Stop at a local tasca for a light snack and your first taste of Algarve wines.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace with a glass of chilled Alvarinho. Dinner at a premium local restaurant in Lagoa or nearby Carvoeiro, easing into the Algarve culinary scene.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack at the hotel upon arrival — charcuterie, local cheeses, and a glass of regional white wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — intimate setting with fresh seafood, grilled sea bass, and an extensive Algarve wine list

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Request an early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. The first evening is intentionally relaxed to allow jet-lag recovery and acclimatization.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim — Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear waters of Praia da Marinha, consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. Arrive early (9:00) to enjoy the coves before crowds build. Bring snorkeling gear to explore the underwater grottos and arches.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the beach, visit the Adega do Cantor winery (owned by Cliff Richard) near Guia for a private premium wine tasting experience. Tour the vineyards, learn about Algarve's unique terroir, and taste their acclaimed Vida Nova and Onda Nova labels paired with local charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the clifftop bar in Carvoeiro village, watching the golden hour light paint the limestone formations. Dinner at a fine dining restaurant in Carvoeiro with views of the sea.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel — freshly baked pastéis de nata, local honey, artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel to enjoy on the beach — smoked salmon wraps, Algarve figs, local almonds, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — acclaimed for its fresh catch of the day, cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), and curated Portuguese wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is a 15-minute drive from Lagoa. Wear sturdy shoes for the cliff walk. Book the Adega do Cantor private tasting in advance — it fills up quickly in September.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Benagil and the famous Benagil Sea Cave by private boat charter departing from Carvoeiro. A luxury speedboat takes you through sea caves, hidden grottos, and secluded coves inaccessible on foot. Swim inside the cathedral-like Algar de Benagil cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Tour the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (castle) with panoramic views over the citrus groves and hills. Explore the Gothic Cathedral and the Museu Arqueológico de Silves.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting dinner in Silves — the region is known for its robust reds. Visit Quinta dos Vales winery for a sunset tasting session featuring their award-winning Grande Escolha and sculpture garden walk before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — açorda de marisco (seafood bread soup), fresh juices, yogurt with Algarve honey and carob
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a beloved terrace restaurant inside the castle walls serving grilled chicken piri-piri, local salads, and regional wines
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui in Silves — legendary seafood restaurant famous for its whole lobster, percebes (barnacles), and extensive wine list; book the private room

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 48 hours in advance. The Benagil cave is best visited in the morning when the light streams through the ceiling opening. Quinta dos Vales requires advance appointment for private tastings.

day_by_day.morning: Private yoga and wellness session on the hotel terrace or garden (9:00–10:30), followed by a 60-minute couples massage or deep tissue treatment at the hotel spa or a nearby luxury wellness center. A slow, indulgent morning to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Praia do Carvalho, a hidden gem accessible through a tunnel carved into the cliff. Spend the afternoon swimming in the sheltered turquoise cove, sunbathing on golden sands, and exploring the rock formations. Bring a premium cooler with chilled wine and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset catamaran cruise departing from Portimão marina. Sail along the stunning coastline with canapés, chilled Champagne, and a knowledgeable skipper pointing out the iconic rock formations of Ponta da Piedade from the sea.

meals.breakfast: Light spa breakfast at the hotel — green smoothies, açaí bowls, poached eggs, avocado toast, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Gourmet beach picnic box from the hotel — lobster rolls, chilled gazpacho, artisan breads, and a bottle of Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — romantic waterfront setting, exceptional fresh fish, and a legendary wine cellar with over 400 Portuguese labels

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Carvalho requires a short walk through a cliff tunnel — wear sandals. The sunset catamaran cruise typically departs around 17:30 in September. Book through the hotel concierge for a fully private charter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres perched on sheer cliffs above the Atlantic. Walk the windswept headland at Cabo de São Vicente, one of Europe's most powerful lighthouses. The raw, elemental beauty here is unlike anywhere else in the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the beaches of Sagres — Praia do Beliche (hidden and dramatic) and Praia da Mareta (wide and golden). Sagres is also a world-class surf destination; arrange a private surf lesson or simply watch the pros ride the Atlantic swells.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the charming fishing village of Sagres before returning to Lagoa. Alternatively, stop in Lagos on the return journey for a vibrant Saturday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — traditional Portuguese spread with local pastries, smoked sausages, regional jams, and freshly squeezed orange juice from Algarve oranges
meals.lunch: Restaurante Dromedário in Sagres — beloved local spot with grilled fish, caldeirada (fish stew), and stunning ocean views from the terrace
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega in Lagos — rustic-chic wine bar and restaurant with an exceptional selection of natural Portuguese wines and creative small plates

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1 hour 15 minutes from Lagoa — consider an early departure (9:00) to maximize time. The wind at Cabo de São Vicente can be very strong; bring a light jacket even in September. Saturday evenings in Lagos are lively — book dinner reservations in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de Silves or Mercado de Lagoa Sunday market — browse local produce, artisan crafts, Algarve honey, carob products, handmade ceramics, and regional delicacies. Stock up on premium local products to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine and food pairing masterclass at a local quinta (estate) near Lagoa. A sommelier guides you through 6–8 premium Algarve wines paired with regional cheeses, smoked fish, charcuterie, and traditional sweets such as Dom Rodrigo and Morgado de Figo.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagoa town — aperitivo at a wine bar, followed by a premium tasting menu dinner at one of the Algarve's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Sunday special with eggs benedict, smoked salmon, freshly baked breads, and Champagne mimosas
meals.lunch: Light tapas at the market or a nearby wine bar in Lagoa — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) with local wines
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Eira do Mel near Cruz de Portugal — Michelin-recommended, celebrated for its creative take on traditional Algarve cuisine and exceptional wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Sunday markets in the Algarve typically run from 8:00 to 13:00. The wine masterclass should be pre-booked through the hotel concierge. This is a slower-paced day intentionally placed mid-trip for recovery and immersion in local culture.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the stunning coastline of Algar Seco in Carvoeiro — a dramatic landscape of sculpted limestone rocks, sea arches, and natural pools carved by the Atlantic. Walk the boardwalk paths and descend to the natural rock pools for a morning swim in crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Quinta da Penina or another premium golf resort near Portimão for a round of golf (optional) or simply enjoy the manicured grounds, pool, and spa facilities as a day guest. Alternatively, arrange a private sailing lesson or paddleboard tour along the Carvoeiro coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at Rooftop Bar at a luxury hotel in Portimão with panoramic views over the marina and Arade River estuary. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Portimão.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light continental spread with local pastries, fruit platters, and specialty Portuguese coffee (bica)
meals.lunch: Tasca da Donzela in Portimão — acclaimed for its cataplana dishes, grilled octopus, and regional wine selection in a charming old-town setting
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic in Portimão — long-standing fine dining institution with exceptional seafood, traditional cataplanas, and one of the best wine lists in the western Algarve

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is a 10-minute drive from Lagoa. The rock formations are best photographed in morning light. Golf at Penina requires advance booking — the Henry Cotton Championship Course is the flagship 18-hole experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Ria Formosa Natural Park near Faro (1 hour east of Lagoa). Depart by 9:00 for a private guided boat tour through the lagoon system, visiting barrier islands, salt pans, and bird sanctuaries. The park is home to flamingos, spoonbills, and the rare purple gallinule.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) — the most remote and pristine barrier island in Ria Formosa. Spend the afternoon on this car-free, near-deserted white sand beach with turquoise shallow waters. Swim, snorkel, and relax in absolute tranquility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro by boat and explore the charming old town (Cidade Velha) — walk the medieval walls, visit the Gothic Sé Cathedral, and enjoy the atmospheric Largo da Sé square before driving back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — energy-focused with eggs, smoked fish, fresh fruit, and strong coffee for the day trip
meals.lunch: Restaurante Estamine on Ilha Deserta — the only restaurant on the island, famous for its grilled fish, clams, and chilled local wines with feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro old town — intimate, acclaimed restaurant in a historic building with creative Portuguese cuisine and an outstanding wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Depart Lagoa by 8:30 to reach Faro in time for the morning boat departure. The Ilha Deserta boat service runs from the Cais da Porta Nova in Faro. Book the private guided Ria Formosa tour in advance. September is ideal for birdwatching as migratory species begin to arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Luxurious spa morning at the hotel or a nearby premium wellness retreat. Indulge in a full spa journey: hammam ritual, hot stone massage, and a Vichy shower treatment. This is a complete rest and restoration morning — no rushing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter tour of the Algarve coastline (departing from Portimão or Faro). A 30–45 minute flight offering breathtaking aerial views of the golden cliffs, hidden beaches, Ria Formosa lagoon, and the Serra de Monchique mountains. A truly once-in-a-lifetime perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at one of the Algarve's top fine dining establishments, marking the midpoint of the trip with a special tasting menu and wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Spa breakfast in bed or on the private balcony — fresh fruit, Greek yogurt with Algarve honey, avocado toast, and herbal infusions
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled sea bream, garden salad, and a glass of premium Alentejo white wine
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc (Porches) — two Michelin stars, chef Hans Neuner's extraordinary tasting menu celebrating the best of Portuguese produce with world-class wine pairings; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Vila Vita Parc's Ocean Restaurant is one of Portugal's most celebrated dining experiences — book 4–6 weeks in advance. The helicopter tour should be arranged through the hotel concierge and is weather-dependent. Vila Vita Parc is only 10 minutes from Lagoa.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Serra de Monchique — the green mountain range rising above the Algarve coast. Drive up to the village of Monchique (850m altitude) through forests of eucalyptus and cork oak. Visit the ruins of the Franciscan convent and explore the artisan village with its famous medronho (arbutus berry) spirit distilleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Fóia peak (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve — for panoramic views stretching from the Atlantic coast to the Alentejo plains on clear days. Visit the thermal spa town of Caldas de Monchique for a soak in the famous mineral springs, used since Roman times.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa via a scenic coastal route. Stop in Portimão for an evening stroll along the riverfront before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Portuguese spread with regional specialties including carob bread, fig jam, and almond pastries from the Monchique region
meals.lunch: Restaurante Luar da Fóia in Monchique — mountain cuisine featuring roasted Alentejo black pork, presunto (cured ham), and local medronho digestif with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — return visit to this waterfront gem for their legendary grilled whole fish and sunset river views

day_by_day.notes: The Serra de Monchique offers a striking contrast to the coastal scenery — temperatures can be 5–8°C cooler at altitude. Purchase a bottle of artisan medronho from a local distillery as a premium souvenir. The drive from Lagoa to Monchique takes approximately 45 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Premium wine estate visit to Herdade dos Grous or a top Alentejo estate near the Algarve border (approximately 1 hour north of Lagoa). Enjoy a private guided vineyard tour, barrel cellar visit, and exclusive tasting of their flagship reserve wines including Moon Harvested and 23 Barricas labels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the coast for an afternoon at Praia de Armação de Pêra — one of the longest and most beautiful beaches in the Algarve. Settle into a premium beach club with sunbeds, parasols, and waiter service. Swim, read, and simply soak up the late-September sun.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar in Armação de Pêra, followed by a memorable seafood dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs any style, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and freshly pressed orange juice
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at the winery — a curated pairing menu of regional Alentejo dishes (migas, black pork, sheep's cheese) with their premium wines served in the estate's private dining room
meals.dinner: Restaurante Atlântico in Armação de Pêra — elegant beachfront dining with fresh lobster, grilled turbot, and an exceptional selection of premium Portuguese wines

day_by_day.notes: The Alentejo wine region begins just north of the Algarve and produces some of Portugal's most celebrated reds. Book the private estate experience well in advance. Armação de Pêra is 15 minutes from Lagoa and has excellent beach infrastructure.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia de Albandeira — one of the most secluded and pristine coves between Lagoa and Armação de Pêra. Arrive early to claim this intimate beach before day visitors arrive. Swim, snorkel among the rocks, and enjoy a final immersive morning in the Algarve's extraordinary coastal beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagoa for a premium souvenir and gift shopping experience — visit artisan shops for hand-painted azulejo tiles, premium Algarve olive oils, local wines, almond and carob confections, and handcrafted leather goods. Pack and prepare for tomorrow's departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — a grand finale celebrating 13 days in the Algarve. Return to Vila Vita Parc or choose another top-tier restaurant for a final extraordinary meal with the finest Portuguese wines.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory hotel breakfast — Champagne, smoked salmon, premium charcuterie, and the full Portuguese spread
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach at Praia de Albandeira — hotel-prepared gourmet box with chilled rosé, fresh seafood, local cheeses, and artisan breads
meals.dinner: Restaurante Henrique Leis in Almancil (45 minutes east) — one Michelin star, legendary chef Henrique Leis' creative Franco-Portuguese cuisine; a bucket-list dining experience to close the trip in style

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Albandeira has limited parking — arrive before 9:30. Restaurante Henrique Leis requires advance reservation and smart casual attire. Consider hiring a driver for the farewell dinner to allow full enjoyment of the wine pairings without driving concerns.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning at the hotel — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take a final stroll through Lagoa town. Visit the local pastelaria for a last pastel de nata and bica (espresso). Pack remaining items and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport. Depending on flight time, stop en route at a final viewpoint or beach for one last look at the Algarve coastline. Arrive at the airport with ample time for a relaxed premium lounge experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry home the finest Algarve wines, artisan products, and memories of 13 extraordinary days on Portugal's golden coast.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — take your time with the full spread, savoring every last Algarve flavor
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge or a final quick lunch at a restaurant near the airport in Faro old town if time permits
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel (typically 12:00; request late checkout until 14:00 if needed). Ensure all purchased wines are properly packed in wine carriers or checked luggage. The private transfer to Faro Airport takes approximately 40–50 minutes from Lagoa. Leave a gratuity for outstanding hotel staff who made the trip exceptional.
